person P id=13 owned by userB (user_id=7), emails=[{"value":"l1fix.b.person.1794106304@example.com","label":"work"}] contact_numbers=[{"value":"555-0100","label":"phone"}]

attack1: userA PUT /admin/leads/attributes/edit/5 (own lead) with person[id]=13 => HTTP 200, leads.person_id now=13 (person owner userB never checked)

sink2: userA GET /admin/leads/get (kanban LeadResource) => HTTP 200; JSON contains personB email=true, phone=true

observed_result_for_record: On the local Docker install (krayin @ ed6deeb), a staff user restricted to view_permission=individual with only the leads.view ACL key successfully issued PUT /admin/leads/attributes/edit/<own-lead-id> with person[id]=<another user's person id>; the request returned HTTP 200 and leads.person_id was persisted to the out-of-scope person (user_id of a different principal). The subsequent GET /admin/leads/view/<lead-id> HTML and GET /admin/leads/get kanban JSON both rendered that person's email address and contact number, while the same user received HTTP 401 when opening the person directly via /admin/contacts/persons/view/<id> and HTTP 401 when targeting the same payload at another user's lead. The bare mass-assignable person_id=<id> request field (no person[] branch) also persisted the link. Fixture users/lead/person rows created for the test were deleted afterwards.
notes: Root cause matches source: LeadRepository::update()/create() resolve person[id] via personRepository->findOrFail() with no bouncer() scope predicate, and Lead::$fillable includes person_id. No deployment-only compensating layer observed (no middleware/policy intercepted the writes).
